abertura: Choose the better meaning for each expression. All six are in the conversation.

itens.t: The teacher can decline a suggestion
itens.porque: Yes. If he cannot, it was never a suggestion — and everything you said before it reads as an instruction.

itens.t: The observer should avoid saying anything critical
itens.porque: No. Feedback with nothing to act on wastes the observation.

itens.t: The observer has to give reasons, not instructions
itens.porque: Yes: the reason is what he can argue with, and arguing with it is how it becomes his.

itens.t: The meeting has no consequences at all
itens.porque: It has consequences — which is why the difference between a reason and an order matters.

itens.t: The teacher has to agree by the end
itens.porque: No. Agreement that is required is not agreement.

itens.t: The observer decides what changes
itens.porque: In this format, no. He does, with your evidence in front of him.

sec1.rationale: If the decision is his, then what you bring has to be arguable. That is not softness -- it is what makes the meeting worth having.

tabela: Opening on the observation
What I noticed was…
Starting on the verdict means he defends before he listens.
Asking first
What were you trying to do at that point?
Your recommendation answers a question he never had.
Recommending refusably
One thing you might try…
He agrees in the room and changes nothing after it.
Holding under disagreement
That is fair — and the part I would still look at is…
Either the point disappears, or the conversation becomes about who is right.

abertura: Three possible answers from the teacher. Which of them is he entitled to?

nota.titulo: He is allowed to disagree with your reading
nota.texto:
What he cannot do is deny what you both saw. What he is entitled to is the
      reason — and about the reason, he knows more than you do.

itens.t: "You need to change the order of those two stages."
itens.porque: The decision is yours: it is an instruction with no room in it.

itens.t: "Have you thought about changing the order?"
itens.porque: His. It puts the same content in a form he can accept, refuse or improve.

itens.t: "Something to think about for next time."
itens.porque: Nobody decides. Softest of the three, and the one most likely to change nothing.

itens.t: "One thing you might try is giving it earlier."
itens.porque: His — and the most useful shape: concrete enough to act on, open enough to decline.

itens.t: "Please make sure the instruction comes first."
itens.porque: Yours, however politely it is phrased. ‘Please’ does not move the decision.

itens.t: "We could look at that again after the next class."
itens.porque: Left open, deliberately. It is the right move when you are not sure yet — and the wrong one when you are.

abertura: Six sentences from feedback meetings. In each one, who is left deciding what happens next?

nota.titulo: Politeness is not the same as room
nota.texto:
Number 5 is the politest sentence in the list and it leaves him nothing to answer. The
      question is never how nice it sounds — it is who is left deciding.

itens: "One thing you {might try|140px} is giving it before they start."
"{Have you thought about|190px} repeating it once they begin?"
"It {might be worth|150px} checking with the slower pairs."
"{That is fair|140px} -- and the part I would still look at is the timing."

itens.porque: The instruction arriving while they worked. Frequency is evidence: three times is a pattern, once is an accident.

itens.t: Happened once, and you saw it
itens.porque: The checking question. He did ask it — and that is why his objection in round two is partly right.

itens.t: Is not in your notes at all
itens.porque: The group finishing early. If it is not in your notes, it cannot go in the feedback: what you do not have, you do not claim.
